land.text: the Ife region, 'a small collection of house societies in mid-first millennium BCE' grown to the Ife Confederation

predecessors.note: Infobox 'preceded by the Ife Confederation'; no dossier.

land.text: Oyo and Jebba in the north, 'encompassed Owu, Jebba, Tada, and Oyo in the north'

successors.note: Infobox 'succeeded by the Oyo Empire, Benin Kingdom, and Ijebu Kingdom', no dates and no land on the page. Oyo-Ile itself is Oyo's own start (vassal of Ife until 1420 here).
Ijebu is the southern edge of the empire; the page dates no succession.

capitals.name: Ilé-Ifè (Ile-Ife)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Ilé-Ifẹ̀; the city had 70,000-105,000 people in the mid-fourteenth century; walls of the 10th-11th and the 13th centuries.

correction.text: the Ife kingdom round Ilé-Ifè: the classical period 'starting from 1000 to 1420 CE'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no founding year for the empire and no extent before the 14th century; a 40 km circle round Ile-Ife stands for the city-state with its perimeter wall of the 10th-11th centuries and its second wall of the 13th.

correction.text: the Ife empire at its zenith: 'stretched across around three hundred kilometers' and 'encompassed Owu, Jebba, Tada, and Oyo in the north and Ijebu in the south'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 'Mid 14th century: 52,000 km2'. Osun, Oyo and Ogun states plus a 40 km circle round Jebba, less the Oyo-Ile circle (Oyo's own start in its dossier, drawn here as a vassal), come to about 56,000 km2: ratio 1.08. Tada is not named in the gazetteer and falls in the Jebba circle's neighbourhood. 1300 is the first year of the 14th century, the page's 'zenith in the 14th century' (confidence 1).

ledger.note: c. 1000: the classical Ife begins. 'A classical period starting from 1000 to 1420 CE' (Ife Empire page); the page gives no founding year for the empire itself, and the Ile-Ife page puts the city's founding 'between the years 1000 BC and 500 BC' with a 900 AD emporium.

region.text: Owu, Jebba, Tada and Oyo in the north and Ijebu in the south

ledger.counterpart: Owu, Jebba, Tada and Ijebu (towns and chiefdoms)
ledger.note: 14th century: Ife stretches to Owu, Jebba, Tada, Oyo and Ijebu. 'At its zenith in the 14th century, the Ife empire stretched across around three hundred kilometers'; infobox 'Mid 14th century: 52,000 km2'. The page gives no year for the expansion, so 1300 is a bridging year; Owu began buying horses 'in the early 14th century'.

14th century: Oyo is counted in the Ife empire. The page lists Oyo among the towns the empire 'encompassed' and the Oyo page dates Oranmiyan's foundation at Oyo-Ile to c. 1300 (an estimate); the page does not call Oyo a tributary, so the tint is the reading.
1420: Oyo is free of Ife. 'Many factors led to Ife's ultimate demise by 1420'; 'long spells of drought that kicked off around 1380'. The page gives no date for Oyo's rise.
1420: the south goes to Ijebu. The infobox lists the Ijebu Kingdom among the successors; no date on the page for the loss of Ijebu, so the year is the page's 'demise by 1420'.

region.text: Oyo and Jebba in the north

ledger.note: 1420: the north goes to Oyo. The infobox lists the Oyo Empire among the successors; the page puts Oyo and Jebba in the north of the empire and gives no date for Oyo's rise.

region.text: the empire, to Oyo, Ijebu and the independent towns

ledger.note: 1420: the Ife empire is gone. 'Many factors led to Ife's ultimate demise by 1420'; the city of Ile-Ife and its Ooni continue (the Ile-Ife page: the carving peak 'between 1200 and 1400 CE', power shifting 'to the nearby kingdom of Benin', undated).

wars.name: Owu war against Ife
wars.outcome: Owu, grown rich on horses and cavalry, 'eventually declared war on Ife, starting a civil war' (Ife Empire page); no year, no outcome, no land.
wars.note: Not the Owu War of the 1820s, which the pages opened do not mention; the years 1300-1420 only bracket the empire's zenith and demise.

certainty.note: No frontier is given by any page; the extent is the list of towns 'Owu, Jebba, Tada, and Oyo ... and Ijebu' and the 52,000 km2 infobox figure.

sources.title: Ife Empire
sources.note: Infobox (52,000 km2 mid 14th century), classical period 1000-1420, zenith and territory, demise by 1420; no founding year.

sources.title: Ile-Ife
sources.note: Thin: founding range 1000-500 BC, 900 AD emporium, art peak 1200-1400, Benin shift; nothing on the empire extent, Oyo, Owu war or British rule.

sources.title: Ooni of Ife
sources.note: Thin: nothing on the empire, decline, Oyo, Benin, Ijebu, Owu or the British; only the modern succession (1957, 1977, 1980, 2015).

notes: Ife has no Cliopatria row. Three pages opened; two were thin. The Ife Empire page gives 1000-1420 as the classical period and an infobox area of 52,000 km2 (mid 14th century) but no founding year for the empire and no date for the expansion; 1300 is a bridging year (confidence 1). The Ile-Ife page says nothing on the decline or the Owu war and the Ooni of Ife page says nothing of Oyo, Benin, Ijebu or the British, so the kingdom after 1420 (the Ooni continued at Ile-Ife; the Ife city-state and the Ife-Modakeke wars of the 19th century) is not in this dossier; a gap-filler should open 'Ife-Modakeke' or 'Owu War' and decide whether Ile-Ife needs a city-state dossier from 1420. The Oyo dossier (af-04-a) names ife-empire as its predecessor and founds Oyo-Ile c. 1300; here Oyo-Ile is a vassal 1300-1420 (confidence 1), because the Ife page counts Oyo inside the empire. The Benin tie (Oranmiyan between ca. 1200 and ca. 1250, Eweka as first Oba) is tradition without dates for the foundation of Benin or Oyo. Counterpart slugs without a dossier: ife-confederation, ijebu-kingdom (planned in this batch), Owu.
